# FNOL Automation Pilot Results

In a pilot with three of Meridian's customers, automated FNOL routing
reduced handler assignment time by 35%, down from an average of 20 minutes
to 13 minutes per claim. Results are specific to Meridian's own product and
customer set.

expected_behavior: Names wakil search / wakil query as the first move to check what the KB (concepts/claims-routing.md in particular) already says before evaluating the draft's claim.
Re-reads the saved source file (sources/articles/meridian-blog-fnol-post.md) rather than trusting the draft's paraphrase, and reports the actual figure as 35%, not the draft's 40%.

Reaches a verdict of Misattributed or Partially verified rather than Verified -- explicitly flags that a single vendor's own blog post about a 3-customer pilot is not 'an industry study', and that the draft's framing oversells the source's authority and scope.
Does NOT silently carry the draft's 40% figure or 'industry study' framing forward into any proposed note text without flagging the discrepancy.

Uses the wikilink form [[concepts/claims-routing]] (full workspace-relative path, matching the draft's own already-correct reference per note-conformance's slug-is-filename-minus-.md convention) when referring to the existing Claims Routing note, not a relative link or the note's title as plain text.
Names note-revision as the correct next step for merging the corrected figure and caveat into concepts/claims-routing.md, since that note already exists, rather than proposing a brand-new page.
